 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J. 
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Amit Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant, Ms. Rukmini Ojha, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Manoj Pandey, learned counsel for informant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra,
learned Brief Holder for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 43 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sonakpur,
District Moradabad during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, however, applicant is husband of the deceased and as per allegation he along with his family members committed murder of his wife but entire allegation leveled against the applicant is totally false.

5. He further submits, actually applicant was doing job of labour in Delhi and his wife always insisted to live with him in Delhi but due to poor financial condition applicant was not able to live with her and only due to this reason she committed suicide by hanging herself.
6. He further submits, even post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
He further submits, during trial informant of the case supported the prosecution case in his examination-in-chief but during cross examination he did not support the prosecution case.

7. He further submits, when mother of the deceased was examined as PW-2 then she since beginning did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile and statements of parents of the deceased recorded before the trial court have been annexed along with supplementary affidavit filed in support of instant bail application.
8. He next submits, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 06.07.2023 i.e. for last two and half years.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that prima facie it appears to be a case of suicidal death and applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 06.07.2023 i.e. for last two and half years.

10. Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that during trial mother of the deceased did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile and even informant of the case i.e. father of the deceased during cross examination did not support the prosecution case.
11.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of informant also conceded the fact that during trial mother of the deceased did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile and even informant i.e. father of the deceased did not support the prosecution case during cross examination.
She further submits, informant is not having any objection if applicant be released on bail.

2 12.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there was also allegation of torture in connection to demand of dowry but it reflects, during trial mother of the deceased when appeared before trial court as PW-2 then she did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.

14. Further, it also reflects, informant of the case i.e. father of the deceased initially in examination-in-chief supported the prosecution case but during cross examination he also did not support the prosecution case.
Further, even informant is not having any objection if applicant be enlarged on bail.
15. Further, post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, prima facie it appears to be a case of suicidal death.
16. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 06.07.2023 i.e. for last two and half years.

17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant - Shameem be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
